name: Moscow
summary_text: Moscow concentrates enforcement activity of the federal anti-LGBT framework: club raids, the arrest of Kotov as the first person charged with *creating* an extremist organisation on LGBT grounds (late December 2024), and the medical and bureaucratic gatekeeping that the 2023 federal transition ban imposes. The Moscow Times' 2025 survey of persecution is titled around "arrests, club raids and extremism charges." A foreign visitor encountering Moscow police faces the federal propaganda-law penalty—up to 15 days' detention and deportation—applied in a jurisdiction with the highest police density and most active venue-level enforcement in the country. The deviation from national (0.12) is approximately 0.03 below. The severity of the law is identical everywhere (it is federal), but Moscow's role as the primary venue for enforcement operations and its concentration of bureaucratic touchpoints (document verification, medical access, hotel registration) materially raise a visitor's probability of encountering active application. Comparable to Orenburg Oblast (0.09), which produced the country's first criminal extremism conviction against a commercial venue; both represent enforcement-active jurisdictions within the uniform federal framework.
